summary:
Team Antariksh Guru built AgniSync, an interactive fire activity dashboard for Almora, Uttarakhand. MODIS and VIIRS detect hotspots at different resolutions, so their raw counts are difficult to compare. We used NASA FIRMS data to count activity on a shared 1 km grid and adjust VIIRS readings to the Aqua MODIS scale. Across 30 months held out from model fitting, the average absolute monthly gap from MODIS fell from 71.2 to 2.5 active cell-days.

The harmonized calendar flagged April 2024 as unusually active. When we compared both sensors against the same ten earlier Aprils, only VIIRS crossed its own 90th-percentile cutoff. Users can open April 25 on the daily map to see the two grid cells where both sensors recorded hotspots and review NASA POWER weather data for context. This helps land managers identify months worth investigating and trace each result back to the satellite observations.
details:
What AgniSync does
AgniSync is an interactive dashboard for exploring satellite-detected fire activity in Almora, Uttarakhand. It brings Aqua MODIS and Suomi NPP VIIRS observations from NASA FIRMS into one monthly calendar spanning 2003–2025. Land managers and researchers can use it to find unusually active months, compare them with the same month in earlier years, and inspect the daily detections behind each result.

How it works
We place both sensors’ detections on the same 1 km grid. Each sensor contributes one active cell-day for every grid cell where it reports a hotspot on a given UTC day. We then use months with complete records from both sensors to estimate how to express VIIRS activity on the Aqua MODIS scale. Across 30 months held out from model fitting, the average absolute monthly gap from MODIS fell from 71.2 to 2.5 active cell-days after adjustment.

What makes it different
AgniSync lets users check whether both sensors support the same conclusion. The harmonized calendar flagged April 2024 as unusually active. When we compared both sensors against the same ten earlier Aprils, only VIIRS crossed its own 90th-percentile cutoff. On April 25, the daily map shows 6 cells with MODIS detections only, 92 with VIIRS detections only, and 2 with detections from both. Users can click a day, filter the map, and download the records and methods behind the selected month.

Tools and design choices
We built the dashboard with Python, Flask, JavaScript, HTML, CSS, and Plotly. We used pandas to process the records, scikit-learn to fit the adjustment, and Shapely and pyproj to prepare the district boundary and grid. We considered differences in sensor resolution, satellite pass timing, cloud cover, and missing records. The dashboard labels incomplete records and shows NASA POWER weather data alongside the historical comparison so users can review the conditions for themselves.
